title: TerraHorn-18 — Why 2× & 4× Coupled Subwoofer Horns Sound Magical
description: Computational proof of mutual radiation impedance loading: comparing 1, 2, and 4 mouth-coupled 2.25 m folded bass horns (plus a 3-Front / 1-Rear Cardioid stack) at identical 80 Vrms per-cabinet drive.
design_notes: Mutual Mouth Loading (`Re(Z_rad)`): A single 0.49 m² horn mouth is acoustically small at 32 Hz (ka = 0.23), reflecting wave energy back down the horn. Stacking 4 mouths creates a 1.96 m² virtual aperture (+ 2pi ground image = 3.92 m²), multiplying real radiation resistance ~3.7x per driver!

Free Extra Sub-Bass & Lower Excursion: Notice on the `SPL vs Uncoupled Baseline` curve how the 4× stack beats naive point-source summation at 28–42 Hz, collapses throat standing-wave ripple, AND lowers per-driver cone excursion near 32 Hz!
CSA 3:1 Cardioid Variant: Turning 1 of the 4 horns backward with 2.65 ms delay + inverted polarity carves a 15 dB quiet zone behind the stack while retaining 3× coupled forward punch.
